Welcome, coaches. Today, we're very lucky to have Frederick Fontaine. Frederick reached a career-high ranking of an ATP of 59 between 1989 and 1998. From 1999 to January of 2011, Frederick worked with Jeremy Shadi, who reached a singles ranking of world number 31. And since January of 2017, Frederick has been the coach of world number nine, Felix Roger Aliasim, and captain of the Canadian Davis Cup team. Welcome, and if you'd like to ask any questions of Frederick, please pop them in below in the Q&A section, and just type them in, and we'll pass them on to Frederick as soon as they come in. But first for me, until we get some questions coming in, you spoke of one of the slides you had, balance, strong self-efficacy, and patience. There's three components of your coaching that you've assumed and learned about since completing your playing days. Can you elaborate on those for us? Yeah, so hi, everyone. Happy to be with you at this conference. And yes, I mean, it's important to have this balance. Can you repeat the question about that? Sorry. So in one of your slides, you had balance being, having humility as a player when you're successful and then resilience during the down periods. Yeah, I think that's an important message that we need to get across, that we're not the factor of our results. Yeah. I really like this sentence about Richard keeping, and you can see this sentence when you get in

in the center court of Wimbledon, how you are going to face the defeat and the victory. I think it's very important when you are like a competitor because tennis, you are traveling and you play tournaments all around the world and all along the year. And if you are like too much attached with the results, then you are going to have too much up and down. Maybe you are going to also lose your direction in one way. So this is very important to stay balanced, to have a strong internal confidence. And this has to be attached, of course, with your capacity of a good plan to work, to every day to try to do your best. This is the real confidence. This is something that is in your control. And of course, the result is the consequence. So this is something that is very important in the education. Of course, with the parents, but also with the coach, because if we are like as a coach, we are too much in the results. And of course, the player is always in the results. He wants to win. He's going to be happy if he's winning. He's not going to be happy if he's losing. That's we know. But at the same time, we have to rebalance that as a coach, as parents, to have this education role to, okay, let's stay calm. Let's focus on the process, because the result is really the consequence of that. And this is something that we have to keep strong. You've obviously read a lot of psychology. That sounds very familiar in terms of growth mindset, Carol Dweck,

and what she's doing, that delayed gratification, the concept of improvement and being patient about it. But when they come off the court after a loss, and that conversation is always incredibly difficult, is there a time and a place where that occurs? And what do you teach the players from their losses? Yeah, of course. And then, like you said, it's a lot of work, you know, so everybody can understand, okay, we have to be calm. We have to focus on the process. This is something that you can find everywhere now in the psychology or in the personal growth. But then after, it's the action. For me, the most important is the action. And so if you're like, like you said, after a loss, for example, you don't, for me, it's very important to start to talk after when the emotions are going down. There is a moment to do that. And this is something that you have to learn by doing it. That's why it's really important for all the coaches to have an understanding in the structure, you know, in the competition, you have to coach your player in the practice, but you have to come to watch them in competition. Like this, you are really going to be in the reality. And then, of course, you are going to do mistakes because sometimes you are going to want to talk too fast to your player, even if it's like the emotions are high for you and for your player. But with the time, step by step, it's a process you will do.
